summary: Not ready. One example fails (AC-06.2.3 replacement income, 'null' vs None). Two open questions are blocking (OQ-registered-partnership, OQ-canton). The tariff-letter rule contradicts the spec's own evidence. Several major dev-refinement questions have no answer: scope of the tariff result and HR view, post-submission edits, and HR pre-fill. Internal identifiers leak into business prose. Many items and stories are inferred, and some trace judgements are only partial.

findings.title: Failing example: replacement-income church tax suffix
findings.why: The example is the only failed simulation. It expects the programming value 'null' where the business meaning is 'no suffix'. The row is also marked ❌ and repeats the denomination column.
findings.evidence: examples AC-06.2.3 / Replacement income: church_tax_suffix = None, expected 'null'. tech_leak and dev_refinement on US-06.2.
findings.action: Rewrite the expected result as 'no suffix' and define it unambiguously, e.g. empty. Remove the duplicate column and the ❌, then re-run the examples.

findings.title: Base tariff H vs A rule contradicts its own evidence
findings.why: AC-06.4.3 and rule.base_tariff_letter say H requires the child in the household plus sole custody or main contributor. Three cited facts give H1N in cases that rule excludes. The derivation and its tests cannot be written until this is settled.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-06.4 (major). Facts F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc0ae9, -dc6ace, -3eb561. trace_judge on rule.base_tariff_letter. The widowed adult-child example omits the '>50% maintenance' answer.
findings.action: Add a decision in decisions.yaml on the exact H vs A conditions. This could be 'counted child' rather than household plus custody. Fix AC-06.4.3 and its examples to match, including the digit 0 or 1.

findings.title: Blocking open question: registered partnership
findings.why: Employees in a registered partnership (e.g. Daniel) cannot be registered correctly. The pension fund list has no such status, and the question affects the spouse data and the source-tax exemption.
findings.evidence: OQ-registered-partnership (blocking: true). It affects civil_status, the spouse items, subject_to_source_tax and calculator_civil_status. OQ-separated is related.
findings.action: Ask Pensionskasse Muster through HR. Record a decision. The interim recommendation is to treat registered partners as Married, with OQ-separated resolved consistently.

findings.title: Blocking open question: pension fund 'Canton' meaning
findings.why: It is unknown whether the canton means residence or work, and what to enter for cross-border employees. The field is required and the list has only Swiss cantons. residence_canton is also named and described as the canton of residence without backing.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton (blocking: true). fact_judge on F-pension_portal-b359c3. trace_judge on item.residence_canton. US-02.4.
findings.action: Get the fund's answer and decide what is entered for residents of Germany and Liechtenstein. Rename or reword the item to match.

findings.title: Scope of the tariff output and HR visibility undefined
findings.why: The spec derives only the tariff letter. It also defines the suffix, the digit and the cross-border swap, and says HR can see results. It never says what is computed, who sees it, or when. Engineering cannot size the feature without this.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-06.4 (major) and US-05.3 AC-05.3.5 (major). US-01.1 (minor, submit and notify flow).
findings.action: Add a decision on the output. Is it the full code, only the letter or nothing? Who sees it? What are the submit and notify semantics? Update the stories or move HR visibility out of scope explicitly.

findings.title: Post-submission changes and answer invalidation unspecified
findings.why: US-03.3 assumes the first working day changes later, but no actor or mechanism is defined. Going back and changing earlier answers can orphan data that data minimisation forbids keeping.
findings.action: Decide who can edit and until when. Decide whether dependent answers are discarded when upstream answers change. Add ACs for both.

findings.title: First working day inputs and start-date rule ambiguous
findings.why: No story covers HR pre-filling the date. Using the actual first working day instead of the contractual start can push the insurance start to the wrong month. The residence-address timing (current vs at start) changes which questions are asked.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-03.1 (major), feature.md insurance rule (major), US-02.3 (major). AC-03.1.2 is untestable as written.
findings.action: Decide whether the date is pre-filled by HR. Decide whether the rule uses the contract start or the first working day, and whether the address is current or as at the start date. Add testable wording.

findings.title: Item expressions and business text do not match their trace
findings.why: Several required_when and asked_when expressions contradict their own business text. Some claims have no cited fact: the 'only if subject' condition, the step order, the Germany/Liechtenstein rows citing missing facts, and the 'sensitive data' note. A developer would build from the expressions.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: spouse_permit_type, has_children, confession, income_type, civil_status, calculator_residence, questionnaire_flow, US-01.2, US-02.4, US-06.1 to US-06.3.
findings.action: Align each expression with its text. Cite the missing hr_transcript facts, or mark the items as decisions. Drop or confirm the unbacked claims.

findings.title: Source-tax rule only partly confirmed
findings.why: The rule decides who sees the whole source-tax section. Anna hedged, and 'here' meaning Switzerland is an assumption. The Liechtenstein result conflicts with HR's 'always subject'. Income type is still modelled as asked.
findings.evidence: OQ-source-tax-rule, OQ-liechtenstein, OQ-income-type. fact_judge on F-hr_transcript-550840 and -5af8d0.
findings.action: Have HR confirm the decision table. Record the product decisions on income type (fixed to earned income) and on which Liechtenstein result counts.

findings.title: Technical identifiers leak into business prose
findings.why: Field and rule ids and UI mechanics appear in acceptance criteria and notes, which turns engineering choices into spec content.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: US-08.1 (address_country), feature.md (insurance_start_date, calculator_civil_status), US-07.2 (Child 1/2 blocks with add/remove).
findings.action: Replace the ids with business terms. State only the need that each child is described separately.
